introduction.body: Check whether you have enough people, understand your critical roles and have plans in place to manage workforce changes and minimise disruption.

questions.label: Do you have enough people to meet your current and future business and project needs?
questions.helpText: Understanding your workforce capacity helps you spot staffing shortages before they affect your business or projects.

positiveMessage.title: Well Staffed!
positiveMessage.body: Your Strength: Your business appears to have the people needed to support your current operations and future work.

recommendation.title: Review Workforce Capacity
recommendation.body:
Opportunity to Improve: Review workloads, overtime, vacancies and any pressure points before taking on additional work.

Understanding your current workforce capacity will help you decide whether you need to recruit, train or reorganise your team to meet future demand.

Learn more about workforce planning.

questions.label: Have you identified the critical workforce roles your business relies on and forecast future workforce requirements?
questions.helpText: Critical roles are the jobs your business can't operate without. These roles often require specialist skills, licences or experience and can be difficult to fill if someone leaves.

positiveMessage.title: Critical Roles Identified!
positiveMessage.body: Your Strength: You understand which roles are critical to your business and are planning ahead for future workforce needs.

recommendation.title: Identify Critical Roles
recommendation.body:
Opportunity to Improve: Identify the roles that are essential to your business and future projects.

Consider:

  • Which roles are hardest to recruit
  • Where skill shortages could affect your business
  • Future staffing needs
  • Training and succession requirements

Planning ahead helps reduce disruption when vacancies occur.

Learn more about workforce planning.

Access the Critical Roles & Succession Planning template to identify critical personnel and develop succession plans.

Access workforce data through ISACNT or Jobs and Skills Australia.

questions.label: Has your business reduced reliance on one or two key people or contractors?
questions.helpText: Relying on a small number of people can increase the risk of delays if they leave or are unavailable.

positiveMessage.title: Low Dependency!
positiveMessage.body: Your Strength: Your workforce structure supports business continuity and reduces the risk of disruptions caused by the loss or unavailability of key people.

recommendation.title: Reduce Key Person Dependency
recommendation.body:
Opportunity to Improve: Identify where important knowledge, skills or responsibilities sit with only one or two people.

Reduce this risk by:

  • Cross-training staff
  • Documenting key processes
  • Sharing knowledge across your team
  • Developing future leaders

Learn more about workforce planning and risk management.

questions.label: Do you have a plan if key people leave your business or are unavailable?
questions.helpText: Staff turnover, retirements and unexpected absences can disrupt your business if no one is ready to step into key roles.

positiveMessage.title: Succession Ready!
positiveMessage.body: Your Strength: You are planning ahead to keep your business running smoothly when workforce changes occur.

recommendation.title: Plan for Succession
recommendation.body:
Opportunity to Improve: Identify your key people and who could step into their role if needed.

Consider:

  • Succession planning
  • Developing future leaders
  • Documenting important processes
  • Cross-training employees
  • Mentoring less experienced staff

Planning ahead helps reduce disruption and protects valuable business knowledge.

Learn more about workforce planning or staff development and training.

Access the available Critical Roles & Succession Planning template to identify critical personnel and develop succession plans.

questions.label: Can your business utilise local or regional workforce capability where projects are delivered?
questions.helpText: Hiring local workers can reduce travel costs, improve workforce stability and create positive outcomes for local communities.

positiveMessage.title: Locally Connected!
positiveMessage.body: Your Strength: Your business is well placed to support local employment and workforce development.

recommendation.title: Build Local Workforce Participation
recommendation.body:
Opportunity to Improve: Look for opportunities to employ local workers wherever possible.

Building relationships with employment providers, training organisations and community groups can help you find local talent and strengthen workforce pipelines.

Consider supporting:

  • Apprenticeships
  • Traineeships
  • Indigenous employment
  • Local training opportunities

Learn more about apprenticeships, traineeships or Remote Australia Employment Services (RAES).

You can also access recruitment support through:

  • Workforce Australia for free recruitment assistance
  • Recruitment agencies for specialist recruitment support

conclusion.body:
Well done in completing this capacity and continuity questionnaire.

Understanding your workforce strengths and risks is an important step in preparing your business for future projects and growth opportunities.

Trying to change or improve everything at once will be difficult. To help:

  • Access the available Workforce Action Plan template
  • Prioritise a small number of workforce actions
  • Focus on high-risk workforce gaps
  • Review workforce readiness regularly
  • Engage with industry, training providers, and workforce partners early

Would you like to speak to a Territory Business Advisor to speak about your results and make a plan of action?
